correctness.rationale: The exact signed hyperbolic polygon-area formula is derived by Stokes’ theorem and independently checked against Gauss--Bonnet. Normalized exponential representations of Dirichlet gaps, a uniform critical-window Taylor expansion with exponential-tail control, and a delta-method central limit theorem give the law and positive variance. Monotonicity, the two endpoint regimes, and both asymptotic expansions are proved analytically. The included program reproduces finite-angle, finite-mean, and variance checks. Assumptions and unproved extensions are explicit.

originality.rationale: The 2014 open-access geometric triangle-area article and the complete 2015 hyperbolic cyclic-polygon paper do not state the random many-vertex radius/logarithm crossover, limiting coverage function, or its Gaussian fluctuation formula. Broader geometric and stochastic checks found no direct implication covering the assessed combined statement. Classical area identities, exponential spacings and the delta method are acknowledged; historical novelty remains provisional.
residual_risks: A sufficiently general triangular-array spacing theorem could mechanically yield the probabilistic part after an independent geometric identification; priority for the complete evaluated crossover was not exhaustively checked.
Some related public findings were accessible only as short database summaries, not full papers; no negative whole-document claim is based on those summaries.
Nonindexed hyperbolic boundary-polygon literature could contain the same critical scaling.

value.rationale: This limit resolves the natural transition at circle radius \(\log n\) between ideal hyperbolic polygons, whose area is at most \((n-2)\pi\), and random polygons occupying nearly the entire containing disk. The strictly invertible critical coverage fraction and its nonzero Gaussian fluctuations are mathematically motivated continuous geometric invariants, beyond an arbitrary finite sample statistic.
